scenario.title: Opening and navigating the workbench
situations: A terminal user wants to open the correct dashboard.
A new user is overwhelmed by pages and raw status.
A user sees no projects, cannot find an action or follows a stale deep link.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Avoid duplicating work-progress lessons; this family owns opening/orientation/routing only.
Board art is an optional customization exposed in help, not a readiness gate; FIRST-USER 25 already skips its setup step.

lessons.title: Open the right place and preserve sign-in privacy
lessons.when: When setup completes or the user asks to open Yoke.
lessons.need: Know which universe/project is open and use the supported UI launch path without exposing token-bearing links in chat or screen-share output.
lessons.surface: UI up/status; active environment; homepage/setup handoff
lessons.gap: Existing launcher is documented; current discovery and token handling are separate implementation questions. Review question: should FIRST-USER 16 + F proof include handoff from both installation paths?

lessons.title: Navigate by the task at hand
lessons.when: On first dashboard visit, first running item or an empty/error page.
lessons.need: Find Strategy, Frontier, Inbox, Shipping and QA when needed; distinguish empty, unavailable and failed reads instead of exploring every page before work.
lessons.surface: Existing workbench pages, overview activation and board read
lessons.gap: Progress surfaces are already mapped; first navigation, empty states and deep-link behavior are not independently traced. Review question: should dashboard explanation and JOURNEYS cues share the same task names?
